summary: Iteration 4: tested shared-password auth, password change/token invalidation, /api/config (masking, keep-empty, clear, validation), AI ping (real Claude), Telegram error paths, auto-review run-now (1 real call, applied={} so nothing to revert), cron webhook (401/200/duplicate/400) + crons.yml, and regressions. Backend tests via public URL: 28/29 passed. The one failure is real: when a 502 goes out through the public ingress, the backend's JSON body is swapped for a Cloudflare HTML page. Frontend fully tested: login (wrong and correct password, show/hide toggle, Enter key), token kept after reload, garbage token sends user to login, settings view switch, all 5 sections, password mismatch check and change+restore, AI test reply, Telegram switch and detect error toast, auto-review Diaria/Semanal save, account shows 500, logout and log back in. All UI flows passed. Everything is back to its starting state (password BlackCat2233@, emergent key, weekly/0/apply, telegram off, chat id '', 6 symbols/all/1.0/3, $500, bot running).

critical.issue: Anyone can get around the brute-force lock. client_ip() trusts the first X-Forwarded-For value, which the client controls. Confirmed: through the public URL I sent 'X-Forwarded-For: 7.7.7.7' and the backend logged the failed attempt as coming from 7.7.7.7, so an attacker can switch to a new fake IP on every request and never hit the 5-attempt lock. Fix: use the last entry (the one the trusted proxy appends) or X-Real-IP, or add a global failure counter as well.

minor.issue: These return HTTP 502 for upstream errors. Through the public preview ingress, a 502 body is replaced with a Cloudflare HTML page, so the frontend gets non-JSON and errMsg() shows a generic 'Request failed with status code 502' instead of the Spanish detail ('Error IA: …invalid x-api-key', the Telegram description). Reproduced: with a bogus key, POST /api/ai/test on localhost:8001 returns JSON 502 'Error IA: …authentication_error', but the public URL returns HTML. Use a status the proxy passes through, e.g. 400/422/424.

A partial alerts dict resets every key you leave out to True instead of keeping its current value. Example: if ai=false is stored and you send {orders:false}, ai becomes true. Merge with store.cfg.telegram_alerts instead of DEFAULT_ALERTS.

_cron_seen is an unbounded in-memory set that is lost on restart. The background asyncio.create_task(run_auto_review) has no exception handling or logging, so a failed scheduled review is silent: no log entry, no Telegram error. Brute-force _attempts is also in-memory and resets on restart.

integration_issues.flow: AI test / Telegram detect with bad token / auto-review failure (via public URL)
integration_issues.issue: Because of the 502 → HTML replacement above, error toasts show a generic axios message instead of the Spanish backend detail.

action_items: HIGH: Fix client_ip() so X-Forwarded-For spoofing can't get around the 5-attempt lock (use the rightmost/trusted entry or X-Real-IP; consider a global rate limit).

Change the upstream-error status for /ai/test, /ai/auto-review, /ai/advise, /telegram/chats, /telegram/test from 502 to one the ingress passes through (e.g. 424 or 400), so the Spanish error detail reaches the UI.
Merge partial telegram_alerts updates with the current saved values, not the defaults.
Wrap the cron background run_auto_review in try/except and write the failure to engine.log.

Each run costs 1 wrong login (cleared by the next successful login), 3 Claude pings and 1 auto-review. test_ai_bogus_key_then_restore fails via the public URL until the 502 status is changed. Cron 'scheduled' stays false while auto_review_last_at is under 20h old.
rca of the issue: 1) Brute-force bypass: auth.client_ip returns fwd.split(',')[0]. The k8s/Cloudflare ingress appends the real IP to whatever X-Forwarded-For the client sent, so index 0 is attacker-controlled. Repro: curl -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 7.7.7.7' POST /api/auth/login with a wrong password, and the backend log shows 'Intento de acceso fallido desde 7.7.7.7'. 2) Generic error toasts: the backend's HTTPException(502) reaches the edge proxy, which replaces 502 responses with its own HTML error page, so error.response.data.detail is undefined in the UI.
